system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Mitel Networks Corporation realized record after going-private acquisition, ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K/20-F; the traceable realized record
> within the fixed outcome window relies on the deregistration filing, EDGAR's filing
> index, and reputable secondary sources describing subsequent corporate transactions.
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- Following the November 30, 2018 closing, the resulting entity "Mitel Networks ULC" filed a Form 15-12B on December 10, 2018, certifying termination of registration of the common shares under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act (and suspension of the duty to file reports under Sections 13/15(d)), recording approximately one holder of record; the filing states that following the closing, the Company amalgamated with Purchaser and became a wholly owned subsidiary of MLN UK HoldCo Limited, a private limited company incorporated in England and Wales. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-345966, Form 15-12B]
- A review of the registrant's (CIK 0001170534) EDGAR filing history finds no Form 10-K, Form 20-F, or any other periodic report filed after the December 10, 2018 Form 15-12B; the last filing of any type recorded for this CIK through the present is the December 10, 2018 Form 15-12B. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001170534&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]
- No source was found indicating that any successor entity in the acquisition structure (e.g., a debt-issuing holding company) separately registered securities and continued periodic SEC reporting after the transaction; the acquired business's financing was structured as private syndicated credit facilities rather than SEC-registered public debt. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-339026, Form 8-K]

## Realized record under private ownership within the fixed window (secondary/press-sourced)
- On November 9, 2021, RingCentral, Inc. and Mitel announced a strategic partnership under which RingCentral paid Mitel $650 million to acquire intellectual property rights and patents covering network and call management, security, and infrastructure, including Mitel's CloudLink technology, and became Mitel's exclusive UCaaS (cloud) partner; as part of the same transaction, Mitel's existing investor group led by affiliates of Searchlight Capital Partners invested $200 million in newly issued RingCentral shares. [SRC: https://ir.ringcentral.com/news/press-release-details/2021/RingCentral-and-Mitel-Announce-Strategic-Partnership-to-Enable-Customers-to-Transition-Seamlessly-to-Cloud-Based-Unified-Business-Communications/default.aspx]
- On October 18, 2022, Mitel entered into an agreement with a majority of its first-lien and second-lien lenders to amend its credit agreements: $156 million of new-money superpriority "first out" term debt (plus a new superpriority revolving facility) was issued to consenting lenders; $603 million of existing First Lien Debt held by consenting lenders was exchanged for $576 million of new "Second Out" debt; and $152 million of existing Second Lien Debt was exchanged for $125 million of new "Third Out" debt; a new Omnibus Intercreditor Agreement established a payment waterfall that contractually subordinated the liens and loans of non-consenting lenders to the new financing structure. [SRC: https://www.hugheshubbard.com/news/mitel-networks-another-development-in-liability-management-transactions]
- Non-consenting lenders subsequently filed suit alleging that the October 2022 amendment violated protections in the pre-existing credit agreements. [SRC: https://www.hugheshubbard.com/news/mitel-networks-another-development-in-liability-management-transactions]

## Beyond the fixed outcome window (noted for context, not counted as the in-window record)
- On March 9, 2025 (approximately six years and three months after the November 2018 closing, outside the ~2021-2023 window), Mitel announced a Chapter 11 restructuring agreement; the restructuring was completed on June 20, 2025, reducing debt by approximately $1.15 billion and annual cash interest expense by approximately $135 million, with approximately $125 million of new funding raised, and with ownership transitioning from Searchlight Capital Partners to a group of the company's former lenders. [SRC: https://www.mitel.com/about/financial-restructuring]

## Items sought but not found within the window
- No source was located reporting a specific revenue, net income/loss, or comparable audited financial-performance scalar for Mitel's overall business within the ~2021-2023 window; because the entity ceased periodic SEC reporting in December 2018, no primary-filing financial scalar is available for this period. [UNVERIFIED]
- Third-party aggregator descriptions of Mitel's credit-facility history within this period (e.g., a reported reduction of an available revolving-credit amount during 2022) were found but could not be traced to a primary source read for this dossier, so they are not cited here as sourced facts. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Mitel Networks Corporation was taken private and deregistered in December 2018, there is no public audited outcome record (10-K/20-F) for the ~2021-2023 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-345966, Form 15-12B]
- Within the fixed window, the traceable realized record shows the business continuing to operate and transacting at scale — divesting cloud/IP technology assets (CloudLink) to RingCentral for $650 million in November 2021 while its private-equity sponsor simultaneously took a $200 million equity stake in the buyer — followed, in October 2022, by a lender-consented "uptier" amendment to its credit agreements that issued new superpriority debt and contractually subordinated non-consenting lenders, a liability-management transaction that drew litigation from the subordinated lenders. [SRC: https://ir.ringcentral.com/news/press-release-details/2021/RingCentral-and-Mitel-Announce-Strategic-Partnership-to-Enable-Customers-to-Transition-Seamlessly-to-Cloud-Based-Unified-Business-Communications/default.aspx] [SRC: https://www.hugheshubbard.com/news/mitel-networks-another-development-in-liability-management-transactions]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on any audited financial-performance scalar for the acquired business within the fixed window: the absence of periodic SEC reporting precludes a primary-sourced determination of revenue, profitability, or comparable trajectory, though the sourced non-financial-statement events above (technology divestiture; credit-agreement amendment with priority subordination) are documented within the window.

[SLICE END]
